receipts.first_text_witness: You just got promoted. Congratulations. Your salary jumped from 38,000 to $50,000 a year. And for about three weeks, you felt like you were finally making it. You updated your LinkedIn, maybe treated yourself to dinner at that restaurant you always walk past but never enter, and started thinking about all the things you could finally afford. Fast forward 6 months, and somehow you're more stressed about money than you were before the raise. Your bank account looks eerily similar to what it used to, except now you have higher monthly payments for things you convinced yourself you deserved. Welcome to the paycheck mirage, where $50,000 somehow feels exactly like being broke with better credit card debt.
receipts.last_text_witness: the math itself. You're not failing at budgeting. You're succeeding at surviving in a system designed to keep you running in place while convincing you that the treadmill is actually a path to somewhere better. The real mirage isn't just the money. It's the promise that working harder and earning more will eventually set you free. When the game is rigged to expand your expenses faster than your income can
